meta.purpose: Templates for the auto-posted LinkedIn feed (/api/feed). Hand-authored. Every number in a post comes from a data file through a ref below; tools/build_posts.py renders data/post-schedule.json and the card images, and tests/test_posts.py proves each number traces to its source.
meta.howTo: Countdown: an event date + offsets (days before/after; weekends move to the Friday before). Release: set 'date' to mark it; it renders only if every 'requires' confidence is met. Rebuild: python3 tools/build_posts.py Cadence: every week is topped up to cadence.perWeek posts on cadence.weekdays (0=Mon) from the rotations, each only inside its validFrom-validUntil window (the shelf life of its data edition). 'definitions' lists numerals that are definitions, not figures (e.g. a survey's firm-size break).

headline.before: {n} days until DOL sets 2026 FUTA credit reductions
headline.today: Today: DOL sets 2026 FUTA credit reductions

countdowns.body:
Nov. 10 is the date the Department of Labor checks which states still owe federal unemployment loans. Employers in those states lose part of their FUTA credit and pay more for 2026.

Base FUTA: {futaNet:pct1} on the first {futaBase:usd0} per employee.
California's statutory step for 2026: an extra {ca:pct1}, an estimate until DOL confirms.

headline.before: {n} days until Maryland FAMLI contributions begin

countdowns.body:
Starting {start:date}, Maryland employers remit FAMLI contributions: {total:pct2} of wages up to the Social Security wage base ({base27:usd0} in 2027).

Employers with {thr:int} or more employees pay at least half ({er:pct2}) and may withhold the rest from pay. That is up to {erMax:usd2} per employee at the wage cap. Smaller employers owe no employer share but must remit what they withhold. Benefits begin by {benefits:date}.
sources: Maryland FAMLI law via Jackson Lewis
countdowns.cta: DC, MD and VA employer costs, side by side

headline.before: {n} days until the Social Security wage base rises to {base27:usd0}

countdowns.body:
On Jan. 1, 2027 the cap on wages subject to the {rate:pct1} employer Social Security tax moves from {base26:usd0} to {base27:usd0}.

For each employee paid above the cap, the employer's maximum Social Security tax goes from {max26:usd2} to {max27:usd2}: {diff:usd2} more per head.
countdowns.cta: See what it does to your payroll

headline.before: {n} days until Virginia's minimum wage rises to {new:usd2}

countdowns.body:
Virginia's minimum wage moves from {cur:usd2} to {new:usd2} an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, then to {next:usd2} on {nextEff:date}.

For a full-time worker at the floor ({hrs:int} hours a year), that is {annual:usd0} more in annual wages, before payroll taxes rise with it.
sources: Office of the Governor of Virginia, HB1/SB1
countdowns.cta: Wage floors for every DMV jurisdiction

variants.body:
If your benefits or PEO agreement renews Jan. 1, check the numbers now, not at signing.

For scale: the average {kffYear:year} employer-sponsored premium is {single:usd0} for single coverage and {family:usd0} for family. Employers carry {singleEr:usd0} and {familyEr:usd0} of that on average.

The Cost Lab puts your own costs next to a PEO quote, with no assumed savings.

Renewal quotes in hand? Put them side by side before Jan. 1.

The average {kffYear:year} employer share of a health premium is {singleEr:usd0} for single coverage and {familyEr:usd0} for family. A fee quoted per employee per month and one quoted as a percent of payroll are not comparable until you convert them.

The Quote Comparator does that for up to three proposals, in your browser.

releases.body:
California employers lose {ca:pct1} of their FUTA credit for 2026, for an effective FUTA rate of {caNet:pct1} on the first {futaBase:usd0}: {caPerHead:usd2} per employee, due with the annual FUTA return.

The Cost Lab and Data Library now use the final figure.

rotations.headline: What one employee costs an employer in {name}, before the extras
rotations.cardTitle: {name}: the base cost of one employee
rotations.cardSub: Average private-sector pay, employer FICA and the employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees.
rotations.body:
In {name}, three numbers every employer cost starts from:

- Average private-sector pay per job: {wage:usd0} a year (includes part-time jobs)
- Employer Social Security and Medicare on that pay ({ficaRate:pct2}): {fica:usd0}
- Employer share of single health coverage at firms under 50 employees: {health:usd0} a year

That is {total:usd0} before unemployment insurance, workers' comp, retirement, admin or a PEO fee. The {name} page carries the rest, each figure with its source.

rotations.shelfLife: QCEW 2025 annual; replaced by the 2026 annual release ~Sept 2027.
rotations.headline: What a {label} job pays in {name}
rotations.cardSub: Average annual pay per job (includes part-time), BLS QCEW 2025, private sector.
rotations.body:
Average pay per {label} job in {name}: {wage:usd0} a year, against {all:usd0} across all private industries (includes part-time jobs).

Employer Social Security and Medicare on that pay: {fica:usd0}. Unemployment insurance, comp and benefits are priced off payroll, so this is the first number to check in any PEO quote.
